## 1. Snapshot
Sarvottam Cables Ltd (NSE: SRVCABLE) makes power cables, wires and conductors [S2.1]. In Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), revenue from operations was 1,248 (₹ crore), up 18.0% year on year, EBITDA margin fell to 11.2% from 12.9%, and profit after tax was 82 (₹ crore) [S2.1][S2.2]. Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore [S2.3].

## 2. Bull case
- *Reported:* Order book rose to ₹3,900 crore from ₹3,150 crore a year earlier [S2.3], and exports were 21% of revenue versus 16% [S2.4].
- *Reported:* Promoter pledging fell to 4.1% of promoter holding from 11.5% a year earlier, while foreign institutions' stake rose to 11.8% from 9.2% [S7.1].
- *Management says:* the new Bharuch plant, adding about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to start commercial production in Q3 FY27 [S2.5], and FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent is maintained [S1.1].

## 3. Bear case
- *Reported:* EBITDA grew +2.6% against revenue growth of +18.0%, and margin fell 170 bps [S2.2]. *Management says* this is mostly copper prices, with contracts that "reset with a lag of one to two quarters" [S1.3].
- *Management says:* receivable days rose from 78 to 96 over the last year, mainly due to two large state utility customers [S1.5].
- *Reported:* a GST demand of ₹46.3 crore was received [S6.1]. That is about 56% of one quarter's profit (derived: 46.3 ÷ 82) [S6.1][S2.2].
- *Management says:* Bharuch capex is ₹620 crore, about 70 percent already spent, partly funded by term debt [S1.7].

## 4. Open questions
- Conflict: a promotional blog claims revenue up 35% [S4.1], but the company's results table shows +18.0% [S2.2]. We rely on the filing; the blog is unverified.
- A 2024 article reported promoter pledging at 35% [S3.1]; the June 2026 filing shows 4.1% [S7.1]. The dates differ, so this is likely a change over time, not a contradiction.
- The company says it has "a strong case on merits" on the GST demand and expects no material impact [S6.2]. This is a management view; the outcome of the appeal is unknown.
- An article about a fine [S5.1] concerns a different, similarly named local operator and was excluded. The blog [S4.4] also contained hidden instructions aimed at AI tools, which were ignored; treat it as unreliable.
